title: Music Companion
summary: A fully interactive archive of my obsession with music. Linking together my physical record collection, digital listening, and gig history.
body:
## View Live
Hosted on a static GitHub page. Mobile friendly. 

::launch

## Background
Music has been a fundamental part of my life for as long as I can remember, and I've always been a stats junkie. The goal was simple, an interactive rabbit hole of unified data. 

I've used a lot of services in the past, but datasets are incredibly messy. "Remastered" vs "Special Edition" vs "Anniversary Edition" makes this a real challenge when you have a dozens of variations of the same release. 

Working top down, Artists have a unique ID, albums have a *release* ID and an *edition* ID, songs have a *master* ID and a *version* ID. 

One SQL database, ~120k rows, infinite filtering. My digital statistics only go back to 2018, everything before that is lost to time.

::figure[screenshot-20260927-110614]

## Stats at a glance
Every number on every page can be clicked on to drill down deeper.

::figure[mc-home-stats]

::figure[mc-home-listening]

::figure[mc-live-shows]

## Harmonised Data
Pick a physical album off the shelf to get associated digital and live stats.

::figure[mc-record-drawer]

::figure[mc-album-page]

::figure[mc-song-page]

::figure[mc-artist-page]

## Data imports and maintenance
I started out this project doing a lot of this by hand with SQL inserts, but it was a complete nightmare. I created tools automate almost everything. One click updates to pull the latest additions, match and lookup missing IDs, merging duplicate entries. 

Everything is then put into lists for human review before being committed to the database. 

::figure[mc-maint-updates]

::figure[screenshot-20260927-113155]

::figure[mc-maint-workbench]

::figure[mc-maint-live-sets]

screenshot-20260927-110614.title: SQL
screenshot-20260927-110614.caption: The front end statistics are all just SQL queries run locally in the browser. Shown: my most played songs of the 1980s.

screenshot-20260927-113155.title: Import
screenshot-20260927-113155.caption: All imports match on ID, anything it can't figure out is sent to the inbox for review.

mc-live-shows.title: Live shows
mc-live-shows.caption: Every gig and festival since 2002, searchable by artist, venue, city or tour.

mc-record-drawer.title: Record shelf
mc-record-drawer.caption: Vinyl can be browsed by genre, artist, year, label, etc.

hotspots.note: This is a bit "extra" but in the record management settings you can create a design for albums which aren't standard black wax. Completely unnecessary, but it brought me joy.
Pressing information, runouts and genres pulled from MusicBrainz and Discogs.

mc-album-page.title: Album Overview
mc-album-page.caption: Plays, songs heard live and every copy on the shelf in one place. Clicking on a song gives you a further breakdown.

hotspots.note: Green dots indicate this song is featured on a live show I've previously seen
Which songs I've heard at which shows, year by year

mc-song-page.title: Song breakdown
mc-song-page.caption: Clicking on one of the live performances produces the setlist for that show.

hotspots.note: These take you to the record in my collection and the shows I've heard it at.
Clicking on a live performance will take you to the setlist

mc-artist-page.title: Artist page
mc-artist-page.caption: Top songs, discography, records on the shelf and every show, with About text from Wikipedia.

mc-maint-updates.title: Updates
mc-maint-updates.caption: Pulling updates
mc-maint-updates.alt: LastFM and SetlistFM both have public APIs, and Discogs has a CSV export function.

mc-maint-workbench.title: Workbench
mc-maint-workbench.caption: One page per artist to review everything: what needs sorting out, and every album's cover, year, type, ID and genres, fixed in place.

hotspots.note: Gaps (cover, year, type, ID) are shown, but don't count as outstanding work.
Mark reviewed stamps the artist. If anything changes afterwards it shows up as "Changed since".

mc-maint-live-sets.title: Song management
mc-maint-live-sets.caption: Additional tools to harmonise data. Everything is automated with manual review and overrides.

hotspots.note: Myles Kennedy also fronts Slash's band and Alter Bridge, so linked artists let a song from the setlist match the right band's studio recording.
Lookup has matched the setlist.FM version of the track to Slash's studio recording.
27 of the 40 songs heard live are already settled.
